REST7900.description:
This unit may be undertaken on either a full-time or part-time basis as part of the Master of Philosophy (MPhil) program.

The MPhil consists of an independent, supervised research program assessed solely through the submission of a thesis.

The research presented for the degree must constitute a substantial and original contribution to scholarship, demonstrating both mastery of the chosen field and a significant advancement of knowledge within that discipline.

Candidates are required to submit a written research proposal within six months of commencement.

The thesis (50,000 words) must be presented in typescript format, unless otherwise approved for alternative examination requirements. It should provide a comprehensive investigation of the chosen topic and make a substantial and original contribution to knowledge. The thesis should also demonstrate relevance to professional practice by extending theoretical foundations into practical applications in education.
REST7900.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate advanced and critical knowledge at the forefront of a discipline or professional field; (2) conceive, design and conduct original research that makes a substantial contribution to knowledge or professional practice; (3) apply advanced research and analytical skills with intellectual independence and ethical responsibility; (4) critically evaluate and synthesise complex concepts, theories, and evidence; (5) communicate research outcomes effectively to specialist and non-specialist audiences; and (6) exercise expert judgement, autonomy, and leadership in research and professional contexts.
REST7900.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: MPhil thesis & thesis examination. Further information is available in the unit outline.



This unit is assessed on an ungraded pass/ungraded failed basis. All assessment items must be successfully completed.

Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
REST7900.contactHours: To maintain satisfactory progress, it is expected that a candidate will commit an average of 30 hours (full-time enrolment) / 15 hours (part-time enrolment) per week towards completion.

REST8900.description:
This unit may be undertaken on either a full-time or part-time basis as part of the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) program.

The PhD consists of an independent, supervised research program assessed solely through the submission of a thesis and completion of a viva voce examination.

The research presented for the degree must constitute a substantial and original contribution to scholarship, demonstrating both mastery of the chosen field and a significant advancement of knowledge within that discipline.

Candidates are required to submit a written research proposal within six months of commencement. Enrolment is initially provisional, with candidature subject to formal confirmation after the first year of study.

The doctoral thesis (approx 80,000 words) must be presented in typescript format, unless otherwise approved for alternative examination requirements. It should provide a comprehensive investigation of the chosen topic and make a substantial and original contribution to knowledge. The thesis should also demonstrate relevance to professional practice by extending theoretical foundations into practical applications in education.
REST8900.outcomes: Students are able to (1) demonstrate advanced and critical knowledge at the forefront of a discipline or professional field; (2) conceive, design and conduct original research that makes a substantial contribution to knowledge or professional practice; (3) apply advanced research and analytical skills with intellectual independence and ethical responsibility; (4) critically evaluate and synthesise complex concepts, theories, and evidence; (5) communicate research outcomes effectively to specialist and non-specialist audiences; and (6) exercise expert judgement, autonomy, and leadership in research and professional contexts.
REST8900.assessment:
Indicative assessments in this unit are as follows: PhD thesis and viva voce examination. Further information is available in the unit outline.



This unit is assessed on an ungraded pass/ungraded failed basis. All assessment items must be successfully completed.

Supplementary assessment is not available in this unit.
REST8900.contactHours: To maintain satisfactory progress, it is expected that a candidate will commit an average of 30 hours (full-time enrolment) / 15 hours (part-time enrolment) per week towards completion.
